import Base

# Each field is one bit-plane of thirty-two independent neighbor counts.
type Tally is Data:
  Tally{ones: U32, twos: U32, fours: U32, eights: U32}

def Tally.add(tally: Tally, +bits: U32) -> Tally:
  match tally:
    case Tally{+ones, +twos, +fours, eights}:
      +carry1 = U32.and(ones, bits)
      +carry2 = U32.and(twos, carry1)
      carry4 = U32.and(fours, carry2)
      Tally{
        U32.xor(ones, bits),
        U32.xor(twos, carry1),
        U32.xor(fours, carry2),
        U32.xor(eights, carry4)
      }

def Tally.row(tally: Tally, +bits: U32) -> Tally:
  Tally.add(
    Tally.add(
      Tally.add(tally, U32.shl(bits)),
      bits),
    U32.shr(bits))

def Tally.flank(tally: Tally, +bits: U32) -> Tally:
  Tally.add(
    Tally.add(tally, U32.shl(bits)),
    U32.shr(bits))

def Life.cell.finish(tally: Tally, here: U32) -> U32:
  match tally:
    case Tally{ones, twos, fours, eights}:
      U32.and(
        twos,
        U32.and(
          U32.not(fours),
          U32.and(U32.not(eights), U32.or(ones, here))))

# Full rows flank the center row: 3 + 2 + 3 is the Moore neighborhood.
def Life.cell(above: U32, +here: U32, below: U32) -> U32:
  Life.cell.finish(
    Tally.row(
      Tally.flank(
        Tally.row(Tally{0, 0, 0, 0}, above),
        here),
      below),
    here)

# Packing is a row-major change of basis from cells to U32 rows.
def Life.pack.row(
  cells: List<&2, U32>, +shift: Nat, word: U32
) -> U32:
  match cells:
    case Nil{}:
      word
    case cell <> rest:
      Life.pack.row(
        rest,
        1n+shift,
        U32.or(word, U32.shln(cell, shift)))

def Life.pack(
  height: Nat, +width: Nat, +cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match height:
    case 0n:
      Nil{}
    case 1n+rest:
      Life.pack.row(List.take(&2, U32, cells, width), 0n, 0)
        <> Life.pack(rest, width, List.drop(&2, U32, cells, width))

def Life.tick(rows: List<&2, U32>, previous: U32) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match rows:
    case Nil{}:
      Nil{}
    case +current <> +rest:
      match rest:
        case Nil{}:
          Life.cell(previous, current, 0) <> Nil{}
        case next <> more:
          Life.cell(previous, current, next)
            <> Life.tick(rest, current)

def Life.unpack.row(width: Nat, +row: U32) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match width:
    case 0n:
      Nil{}
    case 1n+rest:
      U32.and(row, 1) <> Life.unpack.row(rest, U32.shr(row))

def Life.unpack(
  rows: List<&2, U32>, +width: Nat
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match rows:
    case Nil{}:
      Nil{}
    case row <> rest:
      List.append(
        &2,
        U32,
        Life.unpack.row(width, row),
        Life.unpack(rest, width))

def step(
  width: U32, height: U32, cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  +columns = U32.to_nat(width)
  Life.unpack(
    Life.tick(
      Life.pack(U32.to_nat(height), columns, cells),
      0),
    columns)

def evolve(
  turns: Nat, +width: U32, +height: U32, cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match turns:
    case 0n:
      cells
    case 1n+rest:
      evolve(rest, width, height, step(width, height, cells))
hypothesis: Treat each board row as one U32, so the eight-neighbor stencil becomes three shifted votes from the row above, two from the current row, and three from the row below. Accumulate those votes as four bit-planes containing thirty-two independent binary neighbor counts. B3/S23 then collapses to `twos & ~fours & ~eights & (ones | here)`: count three is selected by `ones`, while count two is selected by the live center bit.
findings: Confirmed compiler finding: `Life.cell` destructured the computed result of `Tally.row`, but Bend permits matches and destructuring matches only on parameters or pattern-bound fields. The repair moves that match into `Life.cell.finish`, whose `tally` parameter is a valid scrutinee. The bit-plane algorithm and public contract are unchanged.
